# Propositional Logic Worksheet: Translating Sentences into Symbols

**This document is provided for reference to lecture content, you do not need to submit this problem
set.**

**Notation:** ~ (not), $\wedge$ (and), $\lor$ (or), $\rightarrow$ (if...then), $\leftrightarrow$ (if and only if)

### A note on the conditional

A statement of the form P $\rightarrow$ Q is called a **conditional**. P is called the **antecedent** (the "if" part) and Q is called the **consequent** (the "then" part).

The conditional is only *false* when a true antecedent leads to a false consequent — that is, when the statement makes a promise it doesn't keep. In every other case it is *true*. In particular, **whenever the antecedent is false, the conditional as a whole is true**, regardless of the truth value of the consequent. (Think of it this way: if the antecedent never happens, the conditional's promise is never broken, so it counts as true.)

For each problem below, write your symbolic translation in the blank top cell of the right-hand column of the truth table, then fill in every row below it: the settings of the propositions on the left, and the resulting truth value of your formula on the right.

---

## Worked Example 1

```{=latex}
\begin{minipage}[t]{\textwidth}
\setlength{\parskip}{\smallskipamount}
```

**Statement:** It is raining and it is cold.
**Propositions:** R = it is raining, C = it is cold

**Symbolic form:** R $\wedge$ C

**Truth table:**

```{=latex}
\begingroup
\arrayrulecolor{tblgray}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{6pt}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.05cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.05cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{4.5cm}|}
\hline
R & C & \textbf{R $\wedge$ C} \\ \hline
T & T & T \\ \hline
T & F & F \\ \hline
F & T & F \\ \hline
F & F & F \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\endgroup
\end{minipage}
```

## Worked Example 2

```{=latex}
\begin{minipage}[t]{\textwidth}
\setlength{\parskip}{\smallskipamount}
```

**Statement:** If the alarm sounds, then the building will be evacuated.
**Propositions:** A = the alarm sounds, E = the building is evacuated

**Symbolic form:** A $\rightarrow$ E

Here A (the alarm sounds) is the antecedent and E (the building is evacuated) is the consequent.

**Truth table:**

```{=latex}
\begingroup
\arrayrulecolor{tblgray}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{6pt}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.05cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.05cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{4.5cm}|}
\hline
A & E & \textbf{A $\rightarrow$ E} \\ \hline
T & T & T \\ \hline
T & F & F \\ \hline
F & T & T \\ \hline
F & F & T \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\endgroup
\end{minipage}
```

Notice the last two rows: whenever the antecedent A is false, the conditional is true no matter what E is.
